newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed prices seen holding firm.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed prices seen holding firm.

text.p: Nominal rapeseed prices in Northern Europe should hold up over the next few weeks because of thinning old crop supply, historically high soybean prices and anticipated sunseed shortages, brokers said on Friday.
But they had no trades to report on a day wedged between two holidays.
June delivery old crop free Hamburg was last done at 515 marks a tonne and new crop at 465 marks, basis August.
Initial January-March 1998 negotiations had produced a 492/495 buyer/seller range.
Crushers recently bought some new crop rapeseed for August through October but this activity was limited by seasonally low rapemeal demand in those months, brokers said.
Rape oil at that time of year may also be supplanted by soy oil.
Rainfall in western Europe improved crop prospects and this also discouraged buyers.
May buyers at points other than Hamburg were at 502-510 marks, with June at 510-515 and August at 455-465.
Traders and producers of new crop concluded large numbers of pre-harvest contracts in eastern Germany at farmgate prices of 410-450.
Top prices in the west, where negotiations were less active, were nearer 455 marks.
August rapeseed futures on the Matif exchange last traded at 465 marks, down three on the last close.
Spot rapemeal ex-Hamburg mills was offered at 32.00 marks per 100 kg, with May-first half July at 31.40 and August-October at 26.75.
Rape oil sellers were at 95.50 marks per 100 kg on May and June/July, with August/October oil at 95.00.
